title: Riot’s two game-layer responses: League client hardening and VALORANT visibility
summary: A comparative reading of Riot’s 2018 and 2020 engineering disclosures distinguishes local executable/value obfuscation from server-side withholding of enemy state. Neither design is the Vanguard driver and neither source proves a perfectly opaque client.
author: Observatory editorial
takeaways: League’s bootstrap is about controlling the load of encrypted user-mode client code and dependencies, not kernel interception.
Moving encrypted game values and withholding unrevealed enemy state address different forms of information leakage.
PVS favors optimistic visibility to avoid pop-in, so server withholding is a minimization technique rather than proof that no enemy data is ever exposed.
